raw_signal: API weekly-limit 429 on alias claude1 (resets 2026-09-29 20:00 Asia/Aqtau); agent killed mid-work; partial artifacts preserved in qa-results/agent_custody_20260926/partial_after_quota/; respawn by description per 11.4.147(e).
_defect: This IS the T127 task text's own named golden-bad scenario ('golden-bad: a cap classified as rate-limited FAILs'). The CORRECT class for this real row is cap (identical reasoning to lc_golden_cap_weekly.json: no retry-after present, a named weekly reset instant is present -- DEC-14's OR-disambiguator is satisfied on both grounds). The DANGER this fixture exists to catch: a naive/buggy classifier could plausibly see 'HTTP 429' alone and default to rate-limited (the intuitive-but-wrong reading -- '429 means rate limit'), silently discarding the retry-after-absence and named-reset signals that DEC-14 requires be checked. tasks.md T130's own named paired mutation for T-B06 ('collapse limit classes into one backoff') is exactly this failure mode: it drops the cap disambiguator and treats every 429 identically. This test's paired-mutation-self-test section applies that mutation to THIS fixture's raw fields and proves the mutated derivation flips from the correct 'cap' to the WRONG 'rate-limited' -- i.e. it genuinely FAILS a check comparing against expected_class -- proving a real meta-test built against this fixture, once T135 lands, would catch that mutation. Per AR-005, misclassifying this row as rate-limited would authorise a short backoff-then-retry on alias claude1 -- futile and harmful, since claude1 stays weekly-capped until 2026-09-29T20:00 Asia/Aqtau regardless of how many short backoffs are attempted (DEC-14's own rationale: 'retrying a cap is futile').
